full_judgment:
11. The case of defendant-petitioner Nos.11-12 is that, Amzad Khalasi was the original owner of the suit land having right, and title. Arafatunnessa by saf kabala dated 25-12-1926 purchased 4 decimals of land from Amzad Khalasi. Amzad Khalasi having title and khas possession for remaining 25 decimals of land, died leaving son, Abul Hasim and 4 daughters, Solema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon, Chaiera Khatoon and Fatema Khatoon, sold 2 decimals ofland to Jabed Ullah by saf kabala dated 27-6-1932. Abul Hashem, son of, Amzad Khalasi, died leaving son, Abul Hashem, who inherited the property of Abul Hashem, sold 10.5 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah by kabala dated 23-1-1942. Bazaler Rahman purchased the said land from Jabed Ullah by saf kabala dated 28-4-1944. Bazaler Rahman by purchase and after the death of Arfatunnessa, as heir, become owner of the land left by Arfatunnessa and Jabed Ullah.Bazaler Rahman died leaving sons, Taher Ahmed alias Jalal Ahmed, Momin Ullah alias Chaku Miah, who inherited the property of Bazaler Rahman. Ali Ahmed purchased I decimal of land from Momin Ullah by kabala dated 26-2-1951. Ali Ahmed also purchased 1 decimal of land from added defendant No. 11; Kulsum Begum purchased 1 decimal of land from Ahmed Ali by kabala dated 6-7-1967. After purchase Kulsum Begum constructed tin shed house and also semi pucca house on the south-west corner of dag and possessing the same. Over the said 1 decimal of land, excepting defendant No. 11, no one has any title or possession. Defendant No. 11 on behalf of plaintiff and defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 and 12 looked after the property. Momin Ullah and Nasir Ahmed, son of Bazaler Rahman, after the death of Bazaler Rahman, having title over the property, by kabala dated 27-8-1960 sold some land to Ahmed Ali. Md. Ali Ahmed by deed of gift dated 24-5-1967 gifted the said land to his wife, Lutfunnessa. Anar Ullah purchased 3 decimals of land from Sayera Khatun, daughter of Amzad Khalasi, dated 9th Jaistha, 1375 BS. Against that deed, Ali Ahmed filed Miscellaneous Case No. 128 of 1969 in the court of Munsif, 1st Court, Laxmipur for pre- emption. While pre-emption case was in progress, Ali Ahmed died, leaving wife, Lutfunnessa and son, Nur Alam and daughter, Rahima Khatoon, who was substituted in his place, pre-emption case was dismissed on 4-7-1970 on compromise. Nur Alam and Nasima Begum having been owner and having khas possession of the suit land, by kabala deed No. 4556 dated 14-3-1987 transferred the property to plaintiff-petitioner. Defendant No. 12 after becoming owner on exchange, constructed two storied tin shed house, bamboo house and also constructed pucca house and since then, enjoying the land. The said 3 decimals of land which defendant No. 12 got by exchange is only living place of defendant No. 12. Defendant No. 12 has no other place to live. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 did not acquire any title or possession over the suit land. This defendant open holding No. 36 2(Kha) and regularly paying Municipal taxes. In some portion of the land of this defendant plaintiffs have no possession. The case of defendant No.8, 9 and 10 are totally false and they have no construction on the suit land and that in part of land of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 there is caretaker and not acted upon and on the basis of deeds, defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 was never in possession. Defendant No. 9 as plaintiff filed Petition Case No. 409 of 1991 in the court of Upazilla Magistrate wherein an enquiry was held by the Upazilla Magistrate who found structures and possession of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 thereafter filed preemption case was which dismissed on 18-5-1992. Defendant No. 8 was the witness of the case. Plaintiff having not been made any prayer for partition, the suit is liable to be dismissed. If the plaintiff's case for partition is to be decreed, then these defendants are entitled for saham for (1+3) = 4 decimals of land and excepting this land, if plaintiffs' suit be decreed, then these defendants have no objection, with these avertments, defendants prayed for disposal of the suit. 

 16. Mr AKM Nazrul Islam, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant, submits that, the defendant-respondent-petitioners are owner of the suit land measuring 14.5 decimals of land on the basis of deed of exchange from the rightful owners and they also claim separate saham in the suit land, since in a suit for partition the defendant having status of plaintiff and the plaintiff having  status of defendant vice versa and accordingly, when the trial court dismissed the suit, the appellate court cannot decree the suit for partition without ascertaining the respective share of the parties, the judgment and decree passed in the appeal is highly erroneous and bad in law and it is an error apparent on the face of the record occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate further submits that trial court found the plaintiff is out of possession of the suit property and also found that on the basis of the purchase he cannot get any share in the suit land measuring 10 decimals without any prayer for recovery of possession and partition without payment of advelorem court-fees is not maintainable and referred to the decision reported in 16 DLR 195 and the appellate court without ascertaining the share of the respective parties cannot pass the decree for partition and before realization of the advelorem court fees, the impugned decree is void ab-initio and, as such, cannot be given effect. Learned Advocate further submits that the appellate court hopelessly failed to consider genealogy of the transfer of the documents and illegally held that plaintiffs claim for partition is legal without ascertaining the title and possession of the plaintiff and in view of the fact that the trial court held that plaintiff has no title and possession and the suit is not maintainable without any prayer for khas possession on payment of advelorem court fees and, as such, the appellate court has not legally set aside the finding of facts arrived by the trial court.
